# Baya Weaver Resorts

> Baya Weaver Resorts is a new resort under construction in Old Vythiri, Wayanad, Kerala, India. It will have 14 villas on 3.27 acres of Highland Tea Estate, four of them with private plunge pools, plus an open pool and a clubhouse. The resort is designed by Sumayyasalih Architects and has a target opening of Q4 2026.

Source: https://afinz0z.github.io/Baya-Weaver-Website/  
Last updated: 28 September 2026

## About

Baya Weaver Resorts is being built as an eco-luxury retreat in Old Vythiri, where indigenous architecture, responsible hospitality and the Western Ghats meet in stillness.

Fourteen private villas sit on 3.27 acres of Highland Tea Estate, framed by birdsong and highland sky. Four villas have their own plunge pools, and one open pool serves the wider resort.

Key numbers: 3.27 acres of tea estate; 14 private villas; 4 private pools plus 1 open pool; target opening Q4 2026.

## Features

From land title to ecological ethics, Baya Weaver is built on principles that protect owners, guests and the environment alike.

- **Clear hereditary title**: Janmam clear-title land with zero encumbrances. Documentation is available to verified investors.
- **4 private pools + 1 open pool**: Four villas each have their own plunge pool, not shared and not communal. One open pool serves the wider resort.
- **Eco-responsible design**: Sustainable construction, native landscaping, solar integration and rainwater harvesting.
- **Grand clubhouse**: A central clubhouse designed for dining, gatherings and recreation: the social heart of the resort.
- **National highway access**: Near the NH corridor in Old Vythiri, with road connections to Calicut, Mysore and Bangalore.
- **Strong ROI potential**: Wayanad tourism is among Keralam's fastest-growing segments, with limited comparable eco-luxury supply in Vythiri.

## Construction progress (site update, 22 March 2026)

Construction is under way across the 3.27-acre estate. This is where things stood on 22 March 2026, with photographs from the site that day.

- 6 villas, cluster A: Advanced stage. Roofing and interior finishing in progress.
- 7 villas, cluster B: Structural stage. Foundation and structural framework in progress.
- Internal roads and pathways: Well advanced. Primary access roads laid across the estate.
- Water wells and supply: Complete. Wells dug and operational.
- Electricity connection: Complete. Grid connection secured and live.
- Clubhouse and open pool: Commenced. Site preparation and design finalisation.

## Permits and utilities

All necessary approvals are in place, so the resort is built correctly and transparently as well as beautifully.

- **14 villa permits**: All 14 villa construction permits approved.
- **4 private pools**: Individual pool permits approved for four villas, plus one open pool for the resort.
- **Clubhouse permit**: Central clubhouse and communal facilities approved.
- **Water and power**: Wells operational. Electricity grid connection live.

## The villas

Each villa is designed as a private world, set into the Highland Tea Estate with views across the Western Ghats. Indigenous materials, passive ventilation and Keralam's architectural heritage, brought to contemporary standards by Sumayyasalih Architects.

- 2BHK Pool Villa (architect render)
- Single Bed Villa (architect render)
- Open pool (architect render)
- Grand clubhouse (entrance, dining and recreation. architect render)

## Location

Baya Weaver Resorts is in Old Vythiri (also spelled Vaithiri), in the Wayanad district of Kerala, on the National Highway corridor between Kozhikode and Kalpetta. The 3.27-acre site sits on Highland Tea Estate at about 800 m above sea level, about 67 km (around 1 hour 20 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes by road) from Calicut International Airport.

- **Address**: Old Vythiri, Wayanad District, Kerala 673576. 3.27 acres of Highland Tea Estate on the National Highway corridor.
- **By road**: About 60 km from Kozhikode (Calicut), 150 km from Mysore and 295 km from Bangalore via NH766.
- **Nearest airport**: Calicut International Airport (CCJ), about 67 km or 1 hour 20 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes by road.
- **Elevation and climate**: About 800 m above sea level. Cool mornings, a highland monsoon and crisp winter skies.

### Nearby (independent attractions, not part of the resort)

- **Pookode Lake**: A natural freshwater lake ringed by evergreen forest, in the Vythiri area.
- **Lakkidi View Point**: The viewpoint at the top of the ghat road that climbs into Wayanad from Kozhikode.
- **Chembra Peak**: Wayanad's highest summit. The trek to its heart-shaped lake is iconic.
- **Banasura Sagar Dam**: India's largest earthen dam, ringed by misty hills.
- **Edakkal Caves**: Stone-age petroglyphs high on Ambukuthi Mala.
- **Soochipara Falls**: A 200 ft cascade through rainforest, at its best after the monsoon.
- **Ennooru Tribal Heritage Village**: A place to learn about Adivasi culture and traditions.

## Things to do near Vythiri, Wayanad

Source: https://afinz0z.github.io/Baya-Weaver-Website/wayanad-guide.html (updated 28 September 2026). Drive times are from the resort without traffic. These are independent places; check access before visiting.

### Views and lakes

- **Pookode Lake** (4 min / 3 km): A natural freshwater lake ringed by evergreen forest, in the Vythiri area. Pedal boats are usually available, and a path runs around the water.
- **Lakkidi View Point** (5 min / 4 km): The viewpoint at the top of the ghat road that climbs into Wayanad from Kozhikode, looking down over the hairpin bends and the valleys below. Best early in the morning, before the mist settles or after it lifts.
- **Chain Tree** (5 min / 4 km): A tree bound with an iron chain beside the highway at Lakkidi. Local legend links it to Karinthandan, a tribal guide said to have shown the British the route up the ghat.
- **Neelimala View Point** (50 min / 46 km): A hilltop viewpoint near Vaduvanchal with views across the valley towards Meenmutty Falls. The last stretch is a steep track, usually done by local jeep.
- **Phantom Rock** (40 min / 35 km): A rock formation near Ambalavayal shaped like a skull, with a short climb and wide views over the surrounding plantations.

### Waterfalls

- **Soochipara (Sentinel Rock) Falls** (50 min / 29 km): A three-tiered waterfall near Meppadi, reached by a walk down through tea and forest. The pool at the bottom is popular in the drier months. This area near Chooralmala was affected by the July 2024 landslides. The falls have reopened, but check current access before you go.
- **Meenmutty Falls** (1 h / 47 km): A tall, three-tiered waterfall near Vaduvanchal, reached along a jungle trail. Access has been closed for long periods because of landslide risk. Confirm it is open with the District Tourism Promotion Council (DTPC) before travelling.
- **Kanthanpara Falls** (45 min / 25 km): A smaller, quieter waterfall near Meppadi, with a short walk from the road. A good choice when the bigger falls are busy.
- **Thusharagiri Falls** (30 min / 20 km): A series of cascades in forest on the Kozhikode side of the ghat, at their fullest in the months after the monsoon.

### Treks and peaks

- **Chembra Peak** (1 h 5 min / 29 km): Wayanad’s highest peak, known for the heart-shaped lake on the way up. Treks start from the forest office near Meppadi with a forest department guide. Permits are issued on the day by the forest department, with a daily limit, so start early. Access to the summit has at times been restricted; the lake trek is the usual route.
- **Banasura Hill** (1 h 30 min / 64 km): A longer forest trek above the Banasura Sagar reservoir, with views over the islands in the lake. Usually arranged with a guide through the forest department or DTPC.

### Wildlife

- **Muthanga (Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary)** (45 min / 50 km): Forest department jeep safaris run in a morning and an afternoon slot, with a guide. Elephants, deer and gaur are common sightings; tigers are seen occasionally. Tickets are sold at the forest office on the day and the number of jeeps is limited, so arrive before the slot opens.
- **Tholpetty (Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary)** (1 h 15 min / 62 km): The northern range of the sanctuary, near the Karnataka border, with its own jeep safaris. Pairs well with a visit to Thirunelly Temple. Safaris are limited and run by the forest department; check timings locally.

### Heritage and culture

- **Edakkal Caves** (45 min / 37 km): Rock shelters high on Ambukuthi Mala with carvings thought to date back thousands of years. The final climb is steep and takes most visitors 45 minutes to an hour. Closed on Mondays, in heavy rain, and once the daily visitor limit is reached. Go early.
- **Jain Temple, Sulthan Bathery** (35 min / 36 km): A granite temple thought to date from the 13th century. The town’s name is linked to Tipu Sultan, who is said to have used the temple as an ammunition store.
- **Wayanad Heritage Museum** (35 min / 34 km): A small museum at Ambalavayal with archaeological finds and objects from the district’s tribal communities. Easy to combine with Edakkal Caves and Phantom Rock.
- **Thirunelly Temple** (1 h 5 min / 60 km): An ancient Maha Vishnu temple in the Brahmagiri hills, visited by pilgrims for ancestral rites at the Papanasini stream. Dress modestly and follow temple customs.
- **Pazhassi Tomb, Mananthavady** (45 min / 43 km): The memorial of Pazhassi Raja (Kerala Varma), who led resistance to British rule in the region, with a small museum.
- **En Ooru Tribal Heritage Village** (4 min / 3 km): A tribal heritage village project near Pookode where visitors can learn about the crafts, food and way of life of Wayanad’s tribal communities.
- **Bamboo craft at Thrikkaipetta** (25 min / 25 km): Thrikkaipetta is home to bamboo workshops where you can see local craftspeople at work and buy handmade pieces.

### Rivers, dams and adventure

- **Banasura Sagar Dam** (1 h 30 min / 64 km): India’s largest earth dam, holding back a reservoir scattered with small islands. Speed boats and pedal boats are usually available.
- **Kuruva Island** (50 min / 43 km): A cluster of forested river islands on the Kabani, explored on foot after a bamboo raft or boat crossing run by the forest department and DTPC. Closed through the monsoon and reopened when the river allows; visitor numbers are limited.
- **Karlad Lake** (35 min / 20 km): A lake near Thariode with adventure activities such as a zip line and kayaking, alongside quieter walks.
- **Karapuzha Dam** (30 min / 28 km): An earth dam with landscaped gardens and an adventure park, good for an easy afternoon with children.
- **Kakkayam Dam** (1 h 15 min / 62 km): A forest reservoir on the Kozhikode side, known for its setting in the hills and for boating.

### The coast and Kozhikode

- **Thamarassery Ghat** (40 min / 27 km): The road between Wayanad and Kozhikode winds through nine hairpin bends with views over the forest. Worth driving in daylight. Traffic can back up at weekends and after heavy rain.
- **Kozhikode Beach** (1 h 10 min / 62 km): The city seafront, busy in the evenings with families, sea views and street food stalls.
- **SM Street (Mittai Theruvu), Kozhikode** (1 h 10 min / 61 km): Kozhikode’s old market street, famous for Kozhikode halwa and fresh banana chips.
- **Kappad Beach** (1 h 5 min / 61 km): A quieter beach north of Kozhikode, marked by a monument to Vasco da Gama’s arrival in 1498.

### Food and drink

- **Kozhikode biryani**: Malabar-style dum biryani, made with small-grained rice and cooked sealed so the spices and meat steam together.
- **Pathiri and Malabar breads**: Thin rice-flour flatbreads, eaten with chicken, mutton or fish curries across the Malabar coast.
- **Kappa and curry**: Tapioca, boiled or mashed, served with spicy fish or beef curry. A Kerala staple in small eateries.
- **Puttu, appam and stew**: Breakfast favourites: steamed rice cakes with black chickpea curry, or lacy rice pancakes with a mild coconut stew.
- **Kerala meals**: A full vegetarian lunch of rice with several curries and sides, often served on a banana leaf.
- **Kozhikode halwa and banana chips**: Glossy, chewy halwa in many flavours and chips fried in coconut oil, the classic things to take home.
- **Sulaimani**: Black tea with lemon and spices, the usual after-meal drink in Malabar.
- **Wayanad coffee, tea, pepper and honey**: Wayanad is one of India’s main coffee-growing districts. Local robusta, tea, black pepper, cardamom and forest honey make good gifts.
- **Bamboo rice**: Rice from flowering bamboo, gathered by tribal communities and cooked as porridge or payasam. It is seasonal and not always available.

### Sample days out

- **Half a day close to the resort**: Pookode Lake; Lakkidi View Point and the Chain Tree; En Ooru Tribal Heritage Village. All within about 5 minutes of the resort. A slow morning or a late afternoon.
- **A day of caves, rocks and wildlife**: Edakkal Caves, early (not on a Monday); Phantom Rock; Wayanad Heritage Museum; Jain Temple, Sulthan Bathery; Afternoon jeep safari at Muthanga. The south-east of the district, about 40 to 45 minutes away.
- **A day in north Wayanad**: Kuruva Island (outside the monsoon); Pazhassi Tomb, Mananthavady; Thirunelly Temple; Afternoon safari at Tholpetty. About an hour to an hour and a quarter each way.
- **Lakes, dams and a waterfall**: Karlad Lake; Banasura Sagar Dam; Kanthanpara Falls on the way back. An easy loop with boating and short walks.
- **A day on the coast**: Down the Thamarassery Ghat in daylight; Kozhikode Beach; Lunch in Kozhikode and SM Street; Kappad Beach. About 65 to 75 minutes each way without traffic. Leave early and return before dark.

### When to go

- Monsoon (roughly June to September): heavy rain, green hills and full waterfalls. Some treks, islands and waterfalls close for safety, and roads can be slow.
- After the rains to early spring (roughly October to February): cool, clearer days and the most places open. The busiest time for visitors.
- March to May: warmer and drier. Waterfalls are lower, and early starts are best for treks and safaris.

### Getting around

- A car or taxi is the easiest way to reach most places; local jeeps handle the steeper tracks.
- KSRTC buses connect Kalpetta, Sulthan Bathery, Mananthavady and Kozhikode.
- The Thamarassery Ghat is the main road to Kozhikode and Calicut International Airport. It is slower than the distance suggests.
- On the road to Mysore, the stretch of NH766 through Bandipur is closed to most traffic overnight, so plan to cross in daylight.

### Travelling responsibly

- Stay on marked trails and follow forest department guides and rules.
- Carry your rubbish out. Many forest areas restrict plastic.
- Never feed or approach wild animals, including monkeys at viewpoints.
- Ask before photographing people, especially in tribal settlements, and buy crafts directly from makers where you can.
- Keep away from waterfall edges and fast water, especially after rain.
